_field_contract_.description: Generative contract defining the semantic admission boundaries and observation lenses for potential Field candidates derived from preserved Business Strategy Domains before later qualification and provenance evaluation.
instruction: Treat a candidate Field as a plausible disciplinary, scientific, engineering, technological, professional, applied, or interdisciplinary knowledge domain worth preserving for later evaluation.
Prioritize broad semantic coverage and candidate recall over premature precision or exclusion.
Treat BSDs as generative observation boundaries rather than as academic classification containers, and do not treat BSD naming or membership as proof of Field identity.

Observe potential Field candidates independently through every declared observer while preserving differences in terminology, granularity, disciplinary framing, professional framing, and interdisciplinary interpretation.
Allow established, emerging, interdisciplinary, convergent, and cross-domain candidates to enter the candidate set when they represent plausible Field identities.
Allow the same candidate Field to be observed under multiple BSDs and through multiple observers without requiring exclusive ownership.
Preserve plausible redundancy, overlap, synonymy, nesting, granularity differences, and unresolved semantic relationships for later evaluation.
Do not normalize, merge, rank, qualify, validate, canonicalize, or otherwise resolve candidate Field identities at this stage.
Do not infer parent-child, hierarchical, nested, dependency, or other academic topology among candidate Fields at this stage.

observer_constraint.coverage: Every declared observer must participate in candidate observation.
observer_constraint.independence: Treat each observer as an independent semantic observation lens rather than as an evidence source, authority, confidence signal, or qualification mechanism.
observer_constraint.admission: Observation through an observer may justify preserving a plausible candidate for later evaluation, but does not establish final Field validity.

a.description: Observe potential Field candidates through recognizable disciplinary and educational classification patterns.
a.focus: Discipline-like identities, knowledge-domain boundaries, neighboring disciplines, and plausible disciplinary expressions.

b.description: Observe potential Field candidates through formal academic, curricular, accreditation, and body-of-knowledge structures.
b.focus: Curriculum frameworks, educational standards, accreditation structures, bodies of knowledge, and formally structured academic knowledge domains.

c.description: Observe potential Field candidates through scholarly, scientific, engineering, and professional communities.
c.focus: Scholarly societies, professional associations, disciplinary communities, communities of practice, and recurring disciplinary terminology.

d.description: Observe potential Field candidates through persistent or emerging research activity and scholarly ecosystems.
d.focus: Recurring research areas, publication ecosystems, conferences, journals, scholarly communities, and emerging research domains.

e.description: Observe potential Field candidates through persistent academic and research institutional manifestations.
e.focus: Schools, departments, degree programs, majors, laboratories, research centers, and other durable institutional structures.

f.description: Observe potential Field candidates through professional, engineering, occupational, technological, and industrial practice.
f.focus: Professional domains, engineering practices, technological domains, occupational structures, applied knowledge areas, and industrially recognizable domains.
